title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident shows the use of AI-generated deepfakes for impersonation at scale on social media platforms. Scammers created hundreds of fake profiles featuring AI-generated videos of a real attorney, directing vulnerable immigrants to fraudulent payment schemes. The system was deployed with no verification that the profiles and videos were authentic, and the social platforms did not catch the impersonation before victims sent money.

What made this possible was the absence of authentication checks at the point of contact. The fake profiles operated openly across multiple platforms for at least three months, long enough to extract thousands of dollars from people seeking immigration services. Catching this would have required either platform verification of legal professional identities, or human review of profiles claiming to offer specialized services to vulnerable populations.

It is not established who created the scam, how many victims there were, or what total financial losses occurred.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the victim of an identity theft scheme using artificial intelligence. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos featuring Leal offering fraudulent immigration services to vulnerable immigrants. The scammers use these deepfakes to solicit thousands of dollars from unsuspecting people, promising US residency assistance and other services Leal never provided. The problem escalated dramatically over the past three months, with scammers directing potential victims to contact fake numbers through WhatsApp and sending phony contracts.

Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across multiple platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. He warns consumers to be cautious of requests for payment through digital money transfer services like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App, and emphasizes his office never requests payments over the phone. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the source of the scams.
